description:
Complete the profile lifecycle after the adoption-focused v1.0 foundation by adding local packages, deterministic multi-profile composition, variables, durable semantic ownership, drift-aware reconfiguration, safe upgrades, package capture from live repository state, and portable offline package exchange on top of the shared v1.0 repository-materialization foundation.

## Background

The completed profiles foundation ships repository-local `jit-default` and `jit-dogfood` package directories, minimal list/show/apply and init integration, dry-run planning, package-level provenance, semantic contribution merging, managed assets and regions, overlay validation, recoverable publication, audit events, JSON output, schema exposure, and adopter documentation. Profile packages are data distributed as directories or archives; none is compiled into the binary. This epic owns only the remaining lifecycle and composition delta; it must extend those contracts rather than reimplement the planner, transaction kernel, or projection machinery.

The profiles foundation was apply-only, and that boundary made an applied profile effectively write-once. A repository that edited a profile-owned file in place was reported as drifted, the owning package could not be re-applied once its record existed, and the record itself was verified against the package, so no sanctioned sequence returned such a repository to a valid state. Authoring a package was equally manual: every contribution was hand-written into a manifest, with no operation that read what a working repository already declared. Exchanging a package meant copying a directory with nothing that stated what was copied or confirmed it arrived intact.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Explicitly addressed repository-directory profiles use one versioned package model, work offline, reject a path selector that shadows the id of an explicitly selected recorded profile, and support repeatable ordered profile selection for initialization, application, validation, diff, reconfiguration, and upgrade without remote discovery.
- [hard] REQ-02: Profile dependencies, incompatibilities, compatible JIT ranges, and multi-profile contribution graphs resolve deterministically; missing dependencies, cycles, incompatible selections, unsafe paths or symlinks, undeclared executable assets, and conflicting contributions fail before publication.
- [hard] REQ-03: Multi-profile semantic composition deduplicates identical shared contributions, records shared ownership, and rejects differing definitions without an order-based winner, including type-level conflicts and multiple projections targeting the same managed document.
- [hard] REQ-04: Explicitly non-secret profile variables resolve in the order manifest default, values file, manifest-declared environment variable, then repeatable `--set`, and one declared reference/templating model applies them to supported semantic values and generated text so stored resolved values support deterministic reconfiguration; profiles expose no secret-value input, interpolation, persistence, or audit channel.
- [hard] REQ-05: Repository-local applied-profile records record per-profile worktree-relative package origin, version, compatibility, resolved non-sensitive inputs, package identity, and per-file or per-semantic-key ownership without becoming an authority for declared repository configuration.
- [hard] REQ-06: `jit profile list`, `show`, `validate`, `diff`, `capture`, `pack`, `add`, reapply/reconfigure, and `upgrade` cover applied and explicitly addressed repository-directory packages with stable human output, `--json` envelopes, command/schema exposure, dry-run support for mutations, and audit events that record variable names and source kinds without copying resolved values.
- [hard] REQ-07: Reconfiguration and upgrade use three-way ownership checks: untouched profile-owned content updates, concurrent user/profile changes produce actionable conflicts, shared content retains surviving owners, and only unchanged solely-owned content may be removed as part of an upgrade.
- [hard] REQ-08: Profile lifecycle mutations use the v1.0 shared repository materialization planner and recoverable transaction boundary so complete multi-profile plans, derived repository state, ownership records, and audit events validate and publish atomically, idempotently, and without requiring Git.
- [hard] REQ-09: The distributed repository-local `jit-dogfood` package continues to work without reauthoring package content, duplicating workflow inventories, or weakening config-declared source-of-truth boundaries.
- [hard] REQ-10: Canonical adopter documentation explains local package authoring, capture, package exchange, composition, variables, ownership, drift, reconfiguration, and upgrades while citing or projecting existing profile, rule, gate, and workflow facts rather than copying them.
- [hard] REQ-11: Automated tests cover repository-directory packages, multiple-profile selection and graph resolution, shared and conflicting ownership, non-secret variable precedence, reference rendering, absence of a secret-input surface, reconfiguration, three-way upgrades, capture of new and drifted packages, pack/add round-trip and digest rejection, rollback and recovery, Git-free use, audit output, JSON envelopes, schema exposure, and compatibility with the distributed repository-directory `jit-dogfood` package.
- [hard] REQ-12: Lifecycle capabilities use one canonical directory-package resolver, composition engine, ownership model, and publication path; and each cutover removes the superseded path in the same change, leaving no adapter, dual format, fallback behavior, provenance-only source variant, temporary compatibility code, or duplicated workflow inventory. No pre-release record shape is carried: a repository holding one re-derives its package through capture.
- [hard] REQ-13: Capture produces or refreshes a package tree from the live repository targets a manifest declares, so a repository configured in place becomes an applicable package and a package whose owned content was edited in place is refreshed from that edit; capture reads only declared targets, refuses unsafe paths, links, and undeclared executable content, republishes the tree whole so a source the manifest stopped declaring cannot survive, and emits a tree that decodes and validates as a package.
- [hard] REQ-14: Pack produces one portable archive of a package directory that carries the package identity and a content digest, and add verifies that digest, refuses a mismatched, malformed, or unsafe archive, and places the package inside the worktree ready to apply; both operate offline against a local file with no network access, registry, download, or implicit filesystem search.

## Decisions

- D-01: This work ships in v1.0 and extends the adoption-focused profiles foundation; it does not replace or fork that package, planner, projection, or transaction contract. The apply-only surface is not a smaller lifecycle but an unrecoverable one, so the release waits for the whole of it (`@/charter/D-8`).
- D-02: Package discovery is explicit repository directory first and recorded repository directory on subsequent lifecycle operations, and a package reaches another repository as a portable archive the adopter obtains over a channel they already use and places into the worktree. Remote registries, in-process downloads, implicit filesystem search, and packages embedded in the executable are excluded.
- D-03: Multi-profile composition is semantic and conflict-safe: identical contributions share ownership and different definitions fail without selection-order precedence.
- D-04: Applied records are provenance and ownership evidence, never an alternative source of truth for declared repository configuration.
- D-05: Upgrades may remove unchanged solely-owned content as part of replacing an installed version, but a general profile-removal command is deferred beyond this release.
- D-06: Profile variables are explicitly non-secret and persistable because deterministic reconfiguration requires their resolved values. Packages may configure an environment-variable name as ordinary text, but profiles never receive the referenced runtime secret.
- D-07: Every lifecycle extension must be the long-term SSOT design. No temporary command, record, package, merge, ownership, or publication path may be introduced to stage later cleanup.
- D-08: Authoring and drift resolution share one capture operation over the targets a manifest declares. Rejected: a separate drift-adoption shortcut, because it is sugar over capture and would give one outcome two paths; rejected: leaving hand-written manifests as the only authoring route, because that is what makes an edited profile unrecoverable today.
- D-09: Exchange is an offline pack into a digest-carrying archive plus a digest-verifying add. Rejected: fetching a package from a URL or version-control source, because application stays offline under the charter's offline-package decision and remote-resolution and TLS infrastructure are excluded from the binary by the build-footprint invariant.
- D-10: The profile lifecycle follows the domain-agnostic package-source cutover: `jit-dogfood` is distributed package content rather than binary behavior, and the canonical origin and resolver surface names only worktree-relative directories. Restoring an embedded source, or retaining an embedded provenance value without a resolver, is rejected.

## Risks

- RISK-01: Per-key ownership can become a shadow configuration database; records must describe contribution identity and observed ownership, while final behavior continues to derive from repository registries.
- RISK-02: Three-way upgrades can delete user intent if the base is ambiguous; ownership checks must fail closed when the recorded base is insufficient evidence.
- RISK-03: Users can mistake profile variables for a secret channel; manifests, CLI help, schema, and tests must make the non-secret contract explicit and reject any sensitive-variable declaration or secret indirection surface.
- RISK-04: Composition can duplicate the shared materialization engine; the profiles foundation is an implementation dependency and its shared primitives are the only publication path.
- RISK-05: Capture can widen a package beyond what its manifest declares or carry repository-specific content into a package meant to travel; capture must read only declared targets and must not infer new ones from repository state.
- RISK-06: An archive is a trust boundary; add must verify the recorded digest, reject archive entries that escape the destination or carry unexpected modes, and never publish a partially extracted package.

## Notes

Profile removal, remote package registries, in-process downloads, arbitrary installation hooks, executable-embedded profiles, web UI profile management, and language-specific CI profiles are outside this epic. Portable archives and their verification are in scope; obtaining one is the adopter's own channel. General removal remains deferred beyond this release as confirmed by the owner.
title: Complete profile lifecycle, composition, and upgrades
